synopsis: MTF, PSF, noise and SNR describe image sharpness and cleanliness; the booklet recommends matching virtual and real camera component responses before simulating scenes or trusting virtual detections [f12588, f12589, f12594]. Higher-fidelity camera simulation includes calibrated optical blur, shot and read noise, exposure, saturation and image processing, while thermal-camera validation uses MTF and noise equivalent temperature difference [f4554, f12590]. Darkness modelling requires calibrated noise, exposure and image processing, and signal-level validation should check SNR against rain rate or visibility [f4691, f12591]. Visual realism alone is insufficient: generated images can violate sensor-verification quantities, synthetic scenes can lack real sensor noise, and detectors trained on clean images can fail on noisy or blurred ones [f4904, f3756, f12593]. The evidence includes both a precedent gap—sensor noise was not assessed in the encounter-model comparison discussed at the March 2022 RTCA SC-147 meeting—and a concrete validation example, TaCOS (2024), which checked a simulator noise model against a FLIR camera [f1437, f4755].
